visual_text: CBT for insomnia by phone: one year later
Adults aged 60 and over with insomnia and osteoarthritis pain. No clinically significant insomnia at 12 months, among those followed up.
Six phone sessions of CBT for insomnia: 56 in 100 (67 of 119)
Remission means an Insomnia Severity Index score of 7 or less
McCurry et al., JAMA Intern Med 2021: 327 people, one US health plan
A route that needs the internet leaves some people out
A national study of people living at home in England estimated that about 1 in 5 people aged 60 and over did not use the internet in 2020. The trial did not compare phone with online delivery.
About 1 in 5 did not use the internet (estimate)
Can I have CBT for insomnia by phone or in person?
Kung and Steptoe, Sci Rep 2023; McCurry, JAMA Intern Med 2021
Alasdair MacLullich | Who gets left out
alt_text: Bar chart: no clinically significant insomnia at 12 months, 56 in 100 after six phone sessions of CBT for insomnia (67 of 119) against 26 in 100 with information only (33 of 128). Adults 60 and over with osteoarthritis pain.

Grid of 20 person icons, 4 shaded: about 1 in 5 people aged 60 and over in England did not use the internet in 2020 (estimate). A route needing the internet leaves some out. Ask your GP practice: can I have CBT for insomnia by phone or in person?
